items.title: 'We see plans emptied in weeks': Alarm over remote NDIS recruitment tactics
items.description: People with disabilities in remote Northern Territory communities are being targeted by unscrupulous NDIS providers using high-pressure sales tactics and inducements including cash, cigarettes and alcohol, an ABC investigation can reveal.

items.title: Women's advocate quits Liberal Party after Ley defeat
items.description: Women were less likely to vote for the Coalition at the 2025 election than ever before, according to the Australian Election Study.

items.title: 'I am shocked': Unpacking One Nation's spectacular rise in the polls
items.description: Pauline Hanson's One Nation has seen the fastest polling rise in modern Australian politics. What is going on?

items.title: Taylor lays battle lines on capital gains tax as deputy defends nuclear policy
items.description: Deputy Liberal leader Jane Hume says Australia needs to be "open minded" on nuclear power if the country is to bring down emissions and make power cheaper.

items.title: A millionaire bought a football club while drunk then forgot
items.description: Rob Smethurst was in the throes of a four-day drunken bender when a friend called and told him his local football team was for sale. Now his tiny English club is making global headlines.

items.title: Six mysterious 'Twin Peaks' deaths in Balkan Mountains stir controversy
items.description: Six unsolved deaths in two remote parts of the Balkan Mountains become a source of conspiracy across Bulgaria.

items.title: The right to protest and reasonable police response is under scrutiny
items.description: From 418 arrests in 1977 to fresh clashes in Sydney: The fragility of Australians' right to protest and what makes a reasonable police response is under scrutiny

items.title: Two Hollywood stars, one unconventional family and the talks they never had
items.description: Sophie Hyde's films have won awards at Sundance and Berlin, but she has more riding on her latest release. She's turned the lens on the long-held secrets of her unconventional family.

items.title: Frog toxins the latest poison identified in long line of Russian chemical attacks
items.description: Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny was poisoned by the Kremlin with a rare and lethal toxin found in the skin of poison dart frogs, five European countries have said. It's not the first time the country has been accused of poisoning its enemies.

items.title: A urine test for plastic chemicals set this 25-year-old on a mission to find solutions for pollution
items.description: Kal Glanznig had his urine tested as part of an upcoming documentary exploring plastic pollution in Australia. The results left him speechless.

items.title: PM announces $3.9b 'down payment' towards $30b submarine shipyard
items.description: The South Australian and federal government release plans for the shipyard in Adelaide that will build at least eight nuclear-powered submarines under the AUKUS pact with the US and the UK.

items.title: How 'mortified' Jakara Anthony went from a fall to a second gold medal
items.description: As Jakara Anthony dealt with the disappointment of her singles moguls crash, her coach Peter McNiel was working out how to pick her back up.

items.title: Premier announces extra public holiday for NSW residents
items.description: New South Wales has the fewest public holidays in Australia, observing only 11.

items.title: Obama deplores lack of shame after Trump shares monkey clip
items.description: Former US president Barack Obama has criticised a lack of shame and decorum in the country's political discourse, responding for the first time to a post on Donald Trump's social media account that depicted him and first lady Michelle as monkeys.

items.title: Gisèle Pelicot intends to visit ex-husband in prison to get answers
items.description: Gisèle Pelicot, the woman at the centre of France's largest rape trial, says she intends to visit her ex-husband in jail and look her abuser "straight in the eye" to get answers to other allegations under investigation.

items.title: Man charged after Egyptian artefacts stolen from Caboolture museum
items.description: A 52-year-old man has been charged and 'priceless' Egyptian artefacts have been recovered after a break-in at a small museum in Caboolture on Friday.

items.title: 'Don't be the generation to stuff it up': The reality of running the family business
items.description: Inheriting a family business comes with the weight of generations past. For these change-makers, the future is in modernising their operation and making it their own.

items.title: 'Land on a silver platter': Palestinians reflect on new Israeli West Bank plans
items.description: As Israel's security cabinet agreed on a plan that would pave the way for future settlements in the occupied West Bank, Palestinians say the pressure from Israeli settlers is relentless.

items.title: Liberals fix paralysing uncertainty but morale follows results not reshuffles
items.description: The paralysing uncertainty that weighed on the Liberals' faces has lifted for now, but morale in politics follows results rather than reshuffles.

items.title: Treacherous strait swim the latest step to ocean challenge dream
items.description: Swimming in shark-infested waters across one of the most treacherous island crossings in the world was a challenge Townsville woman Liz Denyer could not pass up.

items.title: Rubio's speech to European allies takes softer tone but sticks to Trump's firm stance
items.description: America's top diplomat uses the Munich Security Conference to call for a renewed partnership between the United States and Europe, with Marco Rubio saying America and Europe "belong together".

items.title: 'Left behind' children paying the price as their mothers work overseas
items.description: A generation of children in South-East Asia are growing up without their mothers, who have to work abroad for decades to make ends meet.

items.title: Why South Molle isn't sharing in the Whitsunday island resort revival
items.description: South Molle Island's former resort has been abandoned since it was damaged by a cyclone in 2017. Now, public access to the island is restricted after Cyclone Koji wreaked havoc on its jetty.

items.title: Statues unveiled of opera star who succeeded before Melba
items.description: An effort to bring new recognition to a Tasmanian opera star who became world famous, but who died poor, culminates in the unveiling of two statues of her in Hobart.

items.title: Aussie quits tennis, pens 'ginormous f*** you' on social media
items.description: Australian tennis player Destanee Aiava says 2026 will be her last year in professional tennis, announcing her impending retirement in an expletive-laden statement on social media.
